flags.why: “Cương vị” belongs to formal speech and writing, as described in this [dictionary entry](https://tudientiengviet.org/cuong-vi/).
“Tót” describes quick movement, not eating a plate of food quickly, consistent with its [dictionary definition](https://vdict.com/t%C3%B3t,3,0,0.html).
flags.fix: Nó chạy tót về nhà. = He dashed home.

flags.why: The quick-movement use in expressions such as “chạy tót” is current everyday Vietnamese.
“Tót” does not mean stubble; its [recorded meanings](https://vdict.com/t%C3%B3t,3,0,0.html) concern position and quick movement.
flags.fix: Delete this sense and its example.

flags.why: The common meaning exhausted or completely depleted, used beyond compounds, is missing from the entry, although it is recorded in the [dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-ki%E1%BB%87t).
flags.fix: Add: adj | exhausted; completely depleted; with nothing left. Example: Vắt kiệt nước trong khăn. = Wring all the water out of the towel.

flags.why: The pleasure sense remains current in contemporary writing rather than being dated, as illustrated by this [2023 publication](https://tapchinghiencuuphathoc.vn/public/uploads/2023/08/Tap-chi-PHAT-HOC-so-4-2023-OUT-IN.compressed.pdf).
“Khoái lạc” names pleasure rather than meaning hedonistic, as reflected in its [noun definition](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-kho%C3%A1i%20l%E1%BA%A1c).
